the-mad-podcast-with-matt-turck.name: The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck
the-mad-podcast-with-matt-turck.bio: Podcast: What Happens When Billions of AI Agents Hit Your Database? (Andy Pavlo)

html_en:
The age of agentic computing is forcing a reckoning across every layer of the stack — from how databases are architected to how we think about software labor itself. Today's dispatches from builders suggest we're past the moment of wondering whether agents will matter, and firmly into the messier question of what happens next.

🗄️ When Agents Meet Databases: The Wild West Gets Wilder

The most technically substantive conversation in today's feed comes from the MAD Podcast, where Matt Turck sat down with Carnegie Mellon database legend Andy Pavlo — now founding ClickHouse Labs — to wrestle with what the agent era actually means for data infrastructure. The vector database bubble, it turns out, was just the opening act.

"Every month, there's a story where someone lost their production database because the agent deleted something. It's the wild west for people that don't know their history of databases. It's just like taking a cheetah, giving them much cocaine, and putting it in a Ferrari." — Andy Pavlo

Pavlo's diagnosis is sharp: vector databases had a real moment, but their moat was always thin. "At the end of the day, it's just an index," he notes, and within a year of ChatGPT's breakout, every major database vendor had shipped their own. Vector search is now table stakes.

The more interesting development is agents creating and branching databases autonomously. When Databricks acquired Neon, a striking stat emerged: the percentage of Neon databases created by agents had jumped from 30% to 80%. Pavlo explains why: coding agents writing new features need to test schema changes against real data, not a toy sample — so they spin up copy-on-write snapshots called branches, validate their changes, and only then promote to production. What was once a careful human-orchestrated process is now being fired off thousands of times a day by automated systems that may or may not know what they're doing.

Watch/Listen: What Happens When Billions of AI Agents Hit Your Database? — The MAD Podcast

🤖 Agents in the Wild: Tax Filings, Tool Calls, and the "We're So Early" Moment

While database researchers worry about the infrastructure implications, builders are shipping — and occasionally marveling at what's already working. @thsottiaux dropped what became one of today's most-liked dispatches: a genuinely mundane, genuinely remarkable account of multi-agent coordination in everyday life.

"My work dot 'Burger' coordinated with my personal dot 'Dorito' over email at my personal dot's request to get documents, which then coordinated with my CPA in order to file some tax stuff. Took 20 minutes. We're still so early." — @thsottiaux

Two personal AI agents, operating across work and personal contexts, coordinating via email with a human accountant to complete a real-world task. The mundanity is the point — this isn't a demo, it's a Tuesday.

Meanwhile, @petergyang offered both a practical tip (a detailed prompt for auditing your sprawling Google app permissions via an AI assistant) and a genuine compliment to Anthropic's engineering team:

"Have to give credit to @amorriscode and team — the Claude Code app is much faster now and arguably simpler to use than ChatGPT. The only things missing still are better browser/computer use, remote control for all threads, and live voice." — @petergyang

💼 The Software Labor Paradox: More Engineers, Not Fewer

Box CEO Aaron Levie offered today's most cogent rebuttal to the "AI will kill software jobs" thesis — and it's worth reading in full. His argument is essentially one of market expansion: automation doesn't shrink a field when it also dramatically expands the addressable surface area of that field.

"The biggest misread of anyone predicting the end of software engineering was imagining that the world only needed a certain amount of software, and bringing automation to the field would reduce the need for labor. Exactly the opposite is happening where essentially most things are actually turning into software... Yes we're not going to be coding manually in the future. But almost everything will be code, which means those that understand it are in a fantastic position." — @levie

This landed 800+ likes for good reason. It's the clearest articulation yet of why the "robots are taking the jobs" frame keeps misfiring in software: the jobs aren't disappearing, the definition of a software problem is simply expanding to encompass trading desks, lab research, and factory floors.

The sentiment found an echo from @thenanyu, who noted that at a recent team offsite, the conversation turned nostalgic: "What did we pay attention to before AI?" "😅 Front end JavaScript frameworks." The speed of the attentional shift in this industry remains disorienting, even to insiders.

📺 Distribution Is Hard, Even for AI-Native Media

A quieter but interesting thread: Swyx pulled back the curtain on the audience mechanics of what appears to be a major AI-focused video channel — over one million unique viewers a month since May, but with stubborn structural challenges.

"We serve >1m unique viewers a month pretty much nonstop since May... but even now 58% of viewers a month are new to us. 68% of viewers not subscribed lol." — @swyx

A massive top-of-funnel, essentially no retention moat. His strategy: lean into "channel affinity" by collaborating with creators whose audiences already overlap — citing Fireship's Jeff Delaney and ThePrimeagen as targets. The AI media landscape, it seems, has the same cold-start problem as every other media category.

⚡ Quick Hits

Replit stays model-agnostic, mostly. After comments at TechCrunch Disrupt sparked confusion, Amjad Masad clarified: "Replit remains model agnostic. Our users can choose Anthropic models as well as many other supported models. What I meant is that OpenAI is now our preferred partner powering Agent based on performance, cost, and strength of our partnership." The distinction between "default" and "only" matters — but the OpenAI partnership signal is notable.

The VC naming arms race continues. @nikunj satirized the proliferation of funding stage labels with a pitch-perfect taxonomy: pre-pre-seed, post-pre-seed, mid-seed, pre-post-seed… "post-post-seed(?)". The joke lands because it's essentially accurate.

On games and AI. Both @rauchg and @petergyang flagged commentary around AI's role in game development, with Guillermo Rauch quoting approvingly: "What matters is the end product, whether it's a game or an engine." The implication: the tools-versus-output debate in creative fields is resolving toward outcomes.
html_zh:
AI智能体正在重塑软件工程的每一个层面——从数据库基础设施到日常税务处理——而这场变革才刚刚开始。

🤖 智能体时代已至：从概念到现实

本周最令人瞩目的现实案例，来自 @thsottiaux。他分享了一段令人印象深刻的日常体验：

"我工作账号的'Burger'智能体和个人账号的'Dorito'智能体通过电子邮件协作，收集文件后交给我的注册会计师，完成了税务申报。全程只花了20分钟。我们还处于非常早期的阶段。"

两个归属于不同身份的AI智能体，自主协调、跨系统沟通、完成真实世界的财务任务——这不是演示，而是日常工作流。他随后低调地补充了一句"Done"，收获了超过六千个点赞。

🗄️ 数据库遇上智能体：混乱与机遇并存

Watch/Listen: The MAD Podcast — What Happens When Billions of AI Agents Hit Your Database? (Andy Pavlo)

如果说智能体是新时代的驾驶员，那数据库就是它们行驶的道路——而这条路正在被高速改造。卡内基梅隆大学教授、ClickHouse Labs创始人 Andy Pavlo 在MAD Podcast中，用一个极具画面感的比喻描述了当前局面：

"对于那些不了解数据库历史的人来说，这就像是野蛮西部。就好像你给一只猎豹喂了大量可卡因，然后把它放进法拉利里。人们开发这些东西的速度快得令人发指。"

Pavlo 指出，两年前"AI与数据库"的交汇点还停留在向量数据库和RAG检索的层面。如今，智能体不仅会查询数据库，还会创建、修改甚至删除数据库。他特别提到了Databricks收购Neon后披露的数据：智能体创建数据库分支（branching）的比例从30%跃升至80%。

"现在人们在用这些编程智能体写新功能、开发应用的新模块，这些工作不再是人类来做了。你需要让智能体在数据库的副本上验证它的修改，而不是直接动生产数据库。"

他也坦言，向量数据库的"护城河"从未真正存在——不到一年，几乎所有主流数据库厂商都内置了向量索引。"它现在是标配，就像表格一样理所当然。"

💼 软件工程的终结？恰恰相反

Aaron Levie 在推特上发表了一篇颇具说服力的长文，直接反驳了"AI将让软件工程师失业"的流行叙事：

"预测软件工程终结的人，最大的误判在于：他们假设世界只需要一定数量的软件，而自动化会减少对劳动力的需求。现实恰恰相反——几乎所有事情都在变成软件……那些从未能被合理数字化的问题，现在都可以用'软件'来解决了。"

他列举了银行交易、生命科学研究、制造业供应链，认为"工程"在经济体系中的重要性只会与日俱增。"是的，我们未来不会手动写代码。但几乎一切都将成为代码，这意味着理解它的人处于绝佳位置。"这与 @thenanyu 的一句玩笑形成呼应——他在团队线下聚会时被问到："我们在AI出现之前关注什么？" 答案是："前端JavaScript框架。😅"

⚙️ 工具赛跑：Claude Code vs ChatGPT，Replit重申立场

Peter Yang 对 Claude Code 的最新进展给出了正面评价：

"不得不给 @amorriscode 和团队点赞——Claude Code 现在速度快了很多，使用上甚至可以说比 ChatGPT 更简洁。目前仍缺少的：更好的浏览器/电脑操控、所有线程的远程控制，以及实时语音。"

与此同时，Replit CEO Amjad Masad 澄清了外界对其合作关系的误读：

"Replit 保持模型无关性。我们的用户可以选择 Anthropic 或其他支持的模型。我在 TC Disrupt 上的意思是，OpenAI 现在是我们 Agent 产品的首选合作伙伴，基于性能、成本和合作关系的综合考量。"

在AI编程工具快速迭代的今天，平台的"模型无关性"承诺与"默认最优体验"之间的张力，正在成为一个微妙的竞争维度。

📊 内容创作者的增长困局，与风投的命名危机

swyx 分享了其内容平台的数据洞察：每月超过100万独立观众，但68%的观众尚未订阅，58%是新面孔。他坦言点击率（CTR）表现欠佳，并把增长希望寄托在与 Fireship、ThePrimeagen 等创作者的联名合作上。规模已经不小，但转化仍是难题——这或许是所有技术内容创作者共同面对的困境。

最后，用 @nikunj 的一则讽刺段子作结——他调侃了当下风险投资轮次命名的混乱：pre-pre-seed、post-pre-seed、mid-seed、pre-post-seed…… 这个行业连给钱起名字都开始需要AI了。
